stem: Which formula gives the fixed overhead volume variance?

options.content: (Actual output - budgeted output) × standard fixed overhead rate per unit
options.rationale: Correct: absorbed overhead less budgeted overhead.

options.content: Budgeted fixed overhead - actual fixed overhead incurred in the same period
options.rationale: That is the expenditure variance.

options.content: (Actual hours - budgeted hours) × rate per hour
options.rationale: That is the capacity sub-variance.
That is an actual cost per unit, not a variance.

explanation: Volume variance = overhead absorbed - budgeted overhead = (actual output - budgeted output) × rate per unit.

stem: Budgeted fixed overhead was US\$14,000 but actual fixed overhead was US\$14,900. What is the expenditure variance?

options.rationale: Spending more than budgeted is adverse.
That is the actual overhead, not the variance.
The percentage rise has been used instead of the difference.

explanation: Expenditure variance = budgeted - actual = -US\$900, adverse.

stem: The fixed overhead capacity variance compares:

options.content: standard hours for actual output with actual hours, at the standard rate per hour
options.rationale: That is the efficiency variance.
That is the expenditure variance.

options.content: actual hours worked with budgeted hours, at the standard rate per hour
options.rationale: Correct: it measures the use of the capacity planned.

options.content: actual units with budgeted units, at the selling price
options.rationale: That is not a fixed overhead variance.

explanation: Capacity: (actual hours - budgeted hours) × standard fixed overhead rate per hour.

stem: Which pair of sub-variances makes up the fixed overhead volume variance?

options.rationale: Expenditure is a separate variance, not part of volume.
Correct: volume = capacity + efficiency.
These are material variances.
Rate is a labour variance.

explanation: Capacity (hours worked v budgeted) plus efficiency (standard hours allowed v hours worked) equals volume.
hints: Volume is split by hours worked and hours allowed.

stem: A brickworks lost two weeks of production because a kiln failed, so it worked far fewer hours than budgeted. Which fixed overhead variance mainly records this?

options.rationale: Expenditure compares spending with budget, not hours.
Efficiency compares hours allowed for the output made with hours worked.
Correct: fewer hours than budgeted.
Less production than budget is adverse.

explanation: Working fewer hours than budgeted leaves capacity unused: an adverse capacity variance.

stem: A firm budgeted fixed overhead of US\$48,000 for 4,000 units (US\$12 a unit) and made 3,700 units. What is the fixed overhead volume variance?

options.rationale: Fewer units than budget under-absorbs overhead: adverse.
That is the overhead absorbed by the 3,700 units.
The unit shortfall must be valued at the rate per unit.
Correct: 300 fewer units × 12.

stem: A factory reports a favourable capacity variance and an adverse efficiency variance of similar size. What is the most likely explanation?

options.content: Fewer hours than budgeted were worked, but they were worked at a very high speed
options.rationale: Fewer hours gives an adverse capacity variance.

options.content: The overhead cost less than budgeted
options.rationale: That affects expenditure, not these two.

options.content: Output was exactly the budgeted amount
options.rationale: The two would then both be explained differently, and volume would be nil.

options.content: More hours than budgeted were worked, but the output took longer than standard
options.rationale: Correct: extra hours were not used productively.

explanation: The workers worked many hours (favourable capacity) but needed more hours than the standard for the output (adverse efficiency).
hints: Capacity is hours worked v budget; efficiency is hours allowed v worked.

stem: The fixed overhead efficiency variance is valued at the actual overhead rate per hour.
explanation: False. It is valued at the standard (budgeted) rate per hour, because the absorption rate is set in advance.
hints: Which rate does an absorbed overhead use?

stem: Match each fixed overhead variance to its formula.

right.content: (Actual output - budgeted output) × rate per unit
(Actual hours - budgeted hours) × rate per hour
(Standard hours for actual output - actual hours) × rate per hour

explanation: Each variance measures a different cause of under- or over-absorption.

stem: Complete the sentence.

payload.template: The capacity variance plus the {{blank:a}} variance equals the {{blank:b}} variance.

explanation: The volume variance is split into capacity and efficiency.

stem: State the formula for the standard fixed overhead absorption rate per hour.

accepted.value: budgeted fixed overhead divided by budgeted hours

explanation: Budgeted fixed overhead ÷ budgeted hours.

modelResponse.text: budgeted fixed overhead divided by budgeted hours

stem: A Bulawayo foundry budgets fixed overhead of US\$21,000 for 7,500 labour hours. Calculate the standard fixed overhead absorption rate per hour.
explanation: 21,000 ÷ 7,500 = US\$2.80 per hour. The rate is set from the budget, not the actual results.
workedSolution: 1. 21,000 ÷ 7,500 = US\$2.80 per hour. The rate is set from the budget, not the actual results.

stem: A Masvingo workshop budgeted fixed overhead of US\$36,400 and actual fixed overhead was US\$38,150. Calculate the fixed overhead expenditure variance (the amount only).
A bakery in Mutare budgeted to make 3,200 batches with a standard fixed overhead rate of US\$5.60 a batch. It made 3,050 batches. Calculate the fixed overhead volume variance (the amount only).
explanation: (3,050 - 3,200) × 5.60 = -840, so US\$840 adverse. Overhead absorbed is 17,080 against a budget of 17,920.
workedSolution: 1. (3,050 - 3,200) × 5.60 = -840, so US\$840 adverse. Overhead absorbed is 17,080 against a budget of 17,920.
hints: The unit difference times the rate per unit.

stem: A Chinhoyi garment factory budgeted 9,600 machine hours with a standard fixed overhead rate of US\$1.20 an hour. Machines were actually run for 9,950 hours. Calculate the capacity variance (the amount only).
explanation: (9,950 - 9,600) × 1.20 = US\$420 favourable, because more hours were used than budgeted. Valuing the 350 hours alone is not enough.
workedSolution: 1. (9,950 - 9,600) × 1.20 = US\$420 favourable, because more hours were used than budgeted. Valuing the 350 hours alone is not enough.
hints: Actual hours less budgeted hours, at the rate per hour.

stem: A joinery in Harare absorbs fixed overhead at US\$2.50 an hour. The output made in a month should have taken 8,820 standard hours, but 9,100 hours were worked. Calculate the fixed overhead efficiency variance (the amount only).
explanation: (8,820 - 9,100) × 2.50 = -700, so US\$700 adverse. The 280 hours over standard are valued at the overhead rate.
workedSolution: 1. (8,820 - 9,100) × 2.50 = -700, so US\$700 adverse. The 280 hours over standard are valued at the overhead rate.
hints: Standard hours allowed less actual hours.

stem: A company under-absorbed fixed overhead by US\$2,300 in total. The expenditure variance was US\$900 adverse. Calculate the fixed overhead volume variance (the amount only).
explanation: Total 2,300 A = expenditure 900 A + volume. Volume = 2,300 - 900 = US\$1,400 adverse. Adding the two (US\$3,200) would double count.
workedSolution: 1. Total 2,300 A = expenditure 900 A + volume. Volume = 2,300 - 900 = US\$1,400 adverse. Adding the two (US\$3,200) would double count.

stem: Explain the difference between the fixed overhead capacity variance and the fixed overhead efficiency variance.

points.description: Capacity compares the hours actually worked with the hours budgeted
Efficiency compares the hours worked with the standard hours allowed for the output made
Capacity shows use of the planned capacity; efficiency shows how productively the hours were used

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The capacity variance compares hours worked with hours budgeted, so it shows whether the factory was busy enough. The efficiency variance compares the hours worked with the standard hours for the output, so it shows how productive the hours were.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem: Explain why a manager responsible for production may not be able to control the fixed overhead expenditure variance.

points.description: Fixed overheads such as rent and depreciation are set by decisions taken at a higher level
They do not change with the activity the production manager controls
A senior manager or the budget holder for the cost should be held accountable instead
Comparing the production manager with a cost he cannot influence would demotivate him

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Rent and depreciation are decided by senior managers and do not vary with production. The expenditure variance should be reported to the person who authorised the cost, not to the production manager.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem: A factory reports a favourable fixed overhead volume variance. Evaluate whether this is good news.

points.description: It means more output than budgeted, so more overhead was absorbed than budgeted
The gain is only an accounting effect: the actual fixed overhead did not change
The extra output must be sold, or inventory and costs rise
A judgement: it is good only if the extra output earns more margin or the hours were used productively (check the efficiency variance)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: More output absorbed more overhead, but actual fixed cost was unchanged, so the gain is only an accounting effect. It is good only if the extra output is sold at a margin and the hours were productive.

explanation: One mark for each point.
hints: Does actual cost change when the volume changes?

stem: Rudo Bricks in Chinhoyi budgeted to make 2,500 batches of bricks at 4 standard labour hours a batch, with fixed overhead of US\$45,000. In the year the business made 2,380 batches, worked 9,800 hours and incurred fixed overhead of US\$46,200. Overhead is absorbed per labour hour.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the standard fixed overhead rate per labour hour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the fixed overhead expenditure variance (amount only).

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the fixed overhead volume variance (amount only).

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Comment on what the capacity and efficiency variances suggest about the year.

points.description: Fewer hours were worked than budgeted, so capacity was not fully used
More hours were taken than the standard allowed for the batches made, so the work was slow
Both reduce overhead absorbed and should be investigated (orders, machine breakdowns, labour skills)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The factory worked 200 fewer hours than budgeted, so some capacity was idle. The batches also needed 280 more hours than the standard allows, so the work was less efficient than planned.

explanation: This item calculates all four fixed overhead variances.

stem: Gweru Plastics budgeted to make 8,000 units at 1.5 standard hours each, with budgeted fixed overhead of US\$60,000. It actually made 8,600 units, worked 12,500 hours and incurred fixed overhead of US\$60,900.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the fixed overhead absorbed by the actual output.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the total over-absorption of fixed overhead.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.explanation: Standard hours = 8,600 × 1.5 = 12,900. (12,900 - 12,500) × 5.00 = US\$2,000 favourable (output took fewer hours than the standard).
parts.workedSolution: 1. Standard hours = 8,600 × 1.5 = 12,900. (12,900 - 12,500) × 5.00 = US\$2,000 favourable (output took fewer hours than the standard).

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why the over-absorption does not mean that fixed costs were controlled well.

points.description: The expenditure variance is adverse (US\$900): actual fixed overhead exceeded the budget
The favourable total comes from higher output, which absorbed more overhead, not from lower costs

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Actual fixed overhead was US\$900 above budget (adverse expenditure). The over-absorption comes from making more than budgeted, which absorbed extra overhead.

explanation: This item analyses an over-absorption into its causes.
hints: Rate per unit = budgeted overhead ÷ budgeted units.
Expenditure + capacity + efficiency should equal the total.
